quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Move back to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign means you must stop. Yield the right-of-way at the intersection. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show your intention.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may be moving into your lane.

questions.question: If you get a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you get a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances when they use sirens or horns and flashing lights. Follow any instructions given by their loudspeaker. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only go when the way is clear.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass you. You should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help the passing vehicle move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows thinking, hurts vision, reduces focus, and slows reaction time. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night driving
Uphill driving

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the force of impact in a crash.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
Usually makes the driver go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react slower to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a driving hazard ahead.

questions.question: When you enter a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before you cross the sidewalk area. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
When your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street when you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can pass quickly enough. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the traffic around you.
Drive at the highest posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull over and stop until the rain stops.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is fine to drive at the highest speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use headlights during the day when you cannot see clearly for 500 feet or less. Use the low beam setting. High beams in fog or rain will bounce light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: It is okay because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can receive a ticket.
Police will always give them a warning instead.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers of cars. Both bicyclists and drivers who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to use a signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and give the proper turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than regular cars.
They do not need extra room to turn and stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Do not stay in these areas. Because trucks are larger and heavier, they need more space to turn and stop than cars do.

questions.question: What can impair a driver's ability to drive safely?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on the driver being healthy and alert. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and tiredness can all affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right where you are.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, clear the path and stop. Slow down and safely pull to the side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can move out of the way.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Use your signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
Use your signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always let other vehicles go first.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: If stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane that matches the arrow direction.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
You can drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always let traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive poorly in ways that look like drunk driving.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive poorly in ways that look like drunk driving.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive poorly in ways that look like drunk driving. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left, but oncoming traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move your car into each lane as soon as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes are clear and it is safe to turn.
